scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0131; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: ‘It takes an hour.’ and ‘The walk takes an hour too.’ are grammatical, natural duration statements.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian copy consistently maps hour to «ساعت» and preserves the sixty-minute time-unit meaning.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: The time-unit target is recognized, practiced in guided dialogue, heard in context, transferred, and retrieved without answer exposure.

distractorQuality.evidence: Time-unit distractors and context alternatives are simple and meaningfully contrast the correct duration.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: سارا و روبی در مسیر خانه زمان رفت‌وآمد با اتوبوس و پیاده را مقایسه می‌کنند.

difficultyFit.evidence: The target noun is concrete and frequent; the duration frame is controlled and supported by context.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: hour recurs across recognition, dialogue, listening, selection, transfer, and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The duration moves from the bus to walking while retaining the same time-unit sense.

overallCoherence.evidence: Outcome, construction, scenario, learner turns, and final retrieval all align to the duration objective.

learnerExperience.evidence: No real learner test is claimed; perceived pacing and ease remain unverified.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the bounded sixty-minute noun sense of hour is reviewed.
Generated audio pronunciation/prosody is not evaluated at this text stage.
resolvedFindings: English grammar and accepted speech consistency were checked.
Persian orthography and translation consistency were checked.
Reference key, part of speech, sense key, and provisional spec hash were cross-checked against the worker packet.
Final retrieval keeps the answer hidden before attempt.
Walking-group story arc returns after 5 Lessons with the learner role switched.
